quest.title: Fulminations and Undercurrents
quest.description: The Wild Hunt has left many secrets behind, and the shadows hidden within the Abyss begin to churn. After chaos strikes, unease spreads amongst people, making them desperate for solutions...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1500, Mora x66000, Hero's Wit x6, Mystic Enhancement Ore x12

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon: Act II
chapter.title: Elegy of Dust and Lamplight

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Make Drinks

dialogues.speaker: Heikki
dialogues.text: The Wild Hunt assault on Starsand Shoal, you mean? Huge wave. First I've ever seen of that size. Good thing it was so brief.

dialogues.speaker: Miemo
dialogues.text: No, no, I mean there's been another, to the north of Nasha Town.

dialogues.speaker: Seppo
dialogues.text: What? How many does that make in the last couple of days now? What are the Lightkeepers playing at...

dialogues.speaker: Miemo
dialogues.text: Can't be helped. There were only a handful stationed on our side in the first place, and the cannon hasn't been fixed yet either. They've been strained to breaking point for a while now, I'll bet.

dialogues.speaker: Heikki
dialogues.text: *sigh* I'm bugging out if this goes on much longer. And here you all told me this was a good place to do business... Fool me once, I say!

dialogues.speaker: Seppo
dialogues.text: Hey now, this could be our big break! My second-eldest brother made his fortune off Wild Hunt attacks, you know. C'mon, let's get moving. There won't be anything left for us if we're late.

dialogues.speaker: Heikki
dialogues.text: Left for us to... scavenge? Mm... I did hear about an overturned cargo vehicle over there...

dialogues.speaker: Miemo
dialogues.text: Hey.

dialogues.speaker: Seppo
dialogues.text: *clears throat*...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... Should've told them that those are dangerous thoughts.

choices.text: Forget it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Guess you're right. Even if we solved this Wild Hunt problem, they'd probably just jump head-first into some new danger if they thought they could earn some quick Mora...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Some self-reflection might not be unwarranted, y'know...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph... Paimon'll have you know that when it comes to staying outta trouble, greed and cowardice make the perfect match!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Should you really be proud of that...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Still, the Wild Hunt's been getting wilder ever since we foiled that mysterious phantom's plan at Starsand Shoal.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (The two of them seem closely connected, and that phantom may very well attack again... even though we know almost nothing about it.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (...In fact, where would we even begin with such an investigation?)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, look — Aino and Ineffa are here in Nasha Town. Ooh, considering what those people said earlier, d'you think they're here to fix that cannon up?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's go say hello.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, dying to know something, aren't ya? You totally zoned out just now...

choices.text: It's like you can read my mind.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hah! Paimon can even guess what you want for dinner... She'll place the orders tonight, don't you worry!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A—Anyway, let's just go, shall we?

choices.text: I was wondering if you'd be willing to carry around the Moon Marrow instead...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? No! Paimon doesn't wanna spend her days running from that thing!

choices.text: I doubt they're the only ones thinking like that.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: #Ah. Familiar faces identified — our good friends, {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Whoa, free manual labor detected!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Those evaluations could not be more different!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Might I ask who this is?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: This is Sousi, Sergeant Major of the nearby Lightkeepers. He's stationed here in this town.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, that means...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: He is Flins's superior, as far as position is considered.

dialogues.speaker: Sousi
dialogues.text: A pleasure to meet you all.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: #This is {NICKNAME} and Paimon, friends of ours. They're experienced adventurers who are new to Nod-Krai.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hi there!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Pleased to meet you. Were you talking about the cannon, by any chance?

dialogues.speaker: Sousi
dialogues.text: Indeed. The sooner we can get it firing again, the quicker we can ease our current... predicament.

dialogues.speaker: Sousi
dialogues.text: Two more Wild Hunt incursions have come sweeping in at different locations after the last one at Starsand Shoal. Our manpower is already stretched, as it is — this is more than we can handle.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hasn't Flins gone back to your HQ to ask for reinforcements? When will they arrive?

dialogues.speaker: Sousi
dialogues.text: Huh. Has he now?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah... That's what he said he was gonna do, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Sousi
dialogues.text: Hmm... He hasn't contacted me about that yet. As per standing orders, he should be leading a team to root out the Wild Hunt, but I haven't received any reports for a while now.

dialogues.speaker: Sousi
dialogues.text: *sigh* Well, he does act outside the remit of his orders sometimes. I'm his superior, yes, but I wouldn't say I have much control over his actions.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So he made the call for backup on his own initiative?

dialogues.speaker: Sousi
dialogues.text: Hard to say. Contacting HQ's a tricky business. I should know, I've tried. They either refuse my requests outright, or end up dragging their feet.

dialogues.speaker: Sousi
dialogues.text: And all the while, we're the ones who have to deal with the Wild Hunt — which, by the way, can strike anywhere in Nod-Krai without warning, sweeping across vast swathes of land. This has been a real test of our endurance, to say the least...

dialogues.speaker: Sousi
dialogues.text: We need to send our personnel where they're needed most. A single missive will not do much to change HQ's attitude, I fear.

dialogues.speaker: Sousi
dialogues.text: Flins understands this well enough, I'm sure.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (He sounds nice enough, but it feels like he's hiding something. This whole spiel sounds like a smokescreen.)

dialogues.speaker: Sousi
dialogues.text: We usually sort our foes ahead of time into ones that our Ratniki will take care of, and ones that we'll target using the cannon.

dialogues.speaker: Sousi
dialogues.text: I've finished the preliminary dispatch work already, but this cannon...

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Okay, okay, okay! "Hurry up, Aino." "Fix this, Aino." You fix it if you're in such a hurry! That, or bring me some snacks. This is tiring work over here!

dialogues.speaker: Sousi
dialogues.text: Ugh... Could you at least tell me how long we'll be delayed? We're way past our scheduled firing time.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Well that's your fault for firing too often recently! Machines get overworked too, you know? You could try thinking about their feelings for once, maybe?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sorry, what? A machine's... feelings?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: In layman's terms, this refers to wear and tear. As such, a machine is more liable to fail the "unhappier" it becomes. The exact probability here would be...

dialogues.speaker: Sousi
dialogues.text: Alright, alright. I'm not good at this stuff, I know that. But let me stress that we Lightkeepers are the primary financial backer of this cannon — and our backing does cover the fees for subsequent repair and maintenance.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Hmph. And I'd say that was a good deal for you! You should thank the Krumkake Craftshop — that means me, by the way — for making you such a huge and powerful weapon for such a measly price!

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Do you even know how much it would've cost you if you'd bought all the parts legit and fresh off the assembly line?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Reminder: Your future snack budget will have to be halved without the long-term commission payment, Aino. Calculating: A viable and cheaper option... Lavender Melon Candy.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: What? No! Absolutely not! I... L—Let me think, alright? It should take, maybe... three more hours?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wouldn't this place be crawling with more monsters than there are Fungi in Sumeru by then!?

dialogues.speaker: Sousi
dialogues.text: That might not be the concern you think it is. The monsters of the Wild Hunt are only active in the immediate vicinity of its attacks. They will not spread any further... on their own initiative, at least.

dialogues.speaker: Sousi
dialogues.text: We Lightkeepers will also keep an eye on those areas, both to monitor the monsters and to prevent people from entering the cannon's blast radius.

dialogues.speaker: Sousi
dialogues.text: That said... I'm afraid I can't wait three hours before dispatching manpower to the locations that the cannon won't be firing on.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: And here's where my need for "manual labor" comes in. There are some checks I haven't finished yet, but with your help, I can get the repairs done sooner.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, but we don't know a thing about this stuff. How much help will we be?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: You'll be fine, trust me! Just take this — oh, and this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, uh, this book is... so heavy... and what is this?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: You can use this Beep-Boopitta to run diagnostics on the cannon. It'll tell you what to do. Oh, and this book will help you understand Beep-Boopitta.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: This cannon was built using more than 50 components from different factories and manufacturers. Aino has bound the manuals into one volume. Also, please note: the device's name is "Birgitta."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: S—So it's manuals all the way down, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Yup. And if you're quick about this, we might just cut our time-to-fire down by a whole two thirds.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We'll do what we can.

dialogues.speaker: Sousi
dialogues.text: I'll go with you.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Nice! So, you'll check the outside, and Ineffa, inside. Come find me in the control room once you're done. Cool? Cool.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Instructions received. Please go about your work seriously as well, Aino. No snacking while I am away.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Hey! A little snacking will also improve my efficiency by two thirds!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aino's explanations for things that don't interest her are a bit... "meh," aren't they? Or is that just how geniuses are?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Isn't Beep-Boopitta just following us around? Sure doesn't seem as smart as she said it is. How are we even supposed to know what to check?

choices.text: We might not be at the right spot yet...

response.speaker: Sousi
response.text: I've watched Ineffa perform routine repairs before. It seems some sort of maintenance port must first be found, and then this small robot will automatically interface with it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, so you're in the know. Nice! What does that port look like?

response.speaker: Sousi
response.text: Now that I'm not so sure of. Let's search around together and see what the robot reacts to.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Works for Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is this it? Hmm, probably not... Or this one? Oh, ew! Stinks of machine oil!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Nope, not here, either...

response.speaker: Sousi
response.text: Hmm, that thing over there looks promising.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Where? Ooh, yeah, it does. Let's try it out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! It's flying...! Does that mean we got it right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, uh... What do we do now?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Lemme give it a try.

choices.text: There's probably some condition we haven't triggered.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, whaddya know? Aino was right. We got this working without understanding a thing Beep-Boopitta said!

dialogues.speaker: Sousi
dialogues.text: Still, it's impressive how you figured things out right away.

choices.text: Benefit of experience, that's all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's up next, along with this stupidly heavy book. Let's see... Should be just like checking a dictionary, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The matching result for this symbol is... "Check passed. All systems normal." Wait, is that it?

response.speaker: Sousi
response.text: Well, as they say, "no news is good news."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, guess you're right. Just feels like we did all this stuff for nothing, that's all... On to the next spot, then.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, Paimon's getting the hang of this now. It's this thing, right?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'll handle it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And this time... Huh? Why are you angry? Oh... Huh, looks like its expressions are also prompts of a kind. Which page is that on...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We need to take note of the order in which its eye colors change — purple, red... Hey, slow down! Paimon didn't catch that!

response.speaker: Birgitta
response.text: Beep-deep— bee-dee-deep—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wha... So now we've got musical prompts too? Weren't you only supposed to be a "beep-boop" machine?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, one final stop. This was quite a trip, huh?

response.speaker: Sousi
response.text: Agreed. I must say, you two have a talent for maintenance work. A bit shaky at points, but not bad for your first job...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Heh, good eye! Paimon's the real deal when she deals for real, y'know!

response.speaker: Sousi
response.text: Really, I'd have liked to share the load, but you were really getting into it, and I didn't want to interrupt.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, couldn't you have mentioned that earlier?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Anyway, let's get this all done in one go.

choices.text: I've figured out puzzles a hundred times more complex before.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Hmm? Weren't you in a hurry to go check stuff?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Go on, now... No dawdling!

dialogues.speaker: Little Robot
dialogues.text: Beep-boop-dee-deep!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What does that mean? Does the book say anything about it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, a pictorial prompt this time... Don't worry, Paimon's just about gotten the hang of which prompts are listed where.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, we gotta take note of the flashing patterns... "1 yellow flash, nothing for 2 seconds, then 2 yellow flashes" means... the components here are overdue for regular maintenance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Maintenance is a high-priority task. The device will be rendered inoperable until it is complete. Switch Beep-Boopitta to Input Mode to send out a signal to unlock components."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The description of Input Mode isn't on this page. Ugh, more page-flipping...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After more page-flipping, then even more page-flipping, Paimon manages to adjust the little robot as instructed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew, that was a real struggle... Well, Paimon needs a break now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good work, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Sousi
dialogues.text: Good work indeed. But it seems this Input Mode requires some additional work to operate.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Allow me.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Checking snack stock... Lower than expected. Please explain, Aino.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Later, later! Can't you see I'm busy... Y'know, saving the poor, anxious inhabitants of this town?

dialogues.speaker: Sousi
dialogues.text: Looks like we're all good. We can remove this thing now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What is it, anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Sousi
dialogues.text: No clue, frankly. But whatever — I got a feeling we've all given up trying to figure this cannon out.

dialogues.speaker: Sousi
dialogues.text: I'll go get the replacement component. We should be done once we pop it in here.

dialogues.speaker: Sousi
dialogues.text: What do you think? Maintenance work's easier than running errands, wouldn't you say?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, that's for sure. We're counting on you, Sousi!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y'know what? Paimon took him for the stony type at first, but he's actually a pretty nice guy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's wait for him here, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Are your tasks complete?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep. Sousi's gone to get the replacement component — we'll be done here once we put it on.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Allow me to check against the recorded data... Yes. This component is approaching its replacement deadline.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: The cannon will generate immense recoil when fired. If this is not controlled, the firing platform will become misaligned. This part is designed to anchor the cannon and ensure accuracy when aiming.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. So if the cannon isn't fixed in place... will it start spinning around like some kind of massive firework?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: A novel analogy... but an apt one. The large-scale damage that might follow would be undesirable by anybody's standards.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: This component is currently easily damaged. The materials are not up to par, and there are still some design flaws. But Aino and I are working to improve it.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Estimated waiting time remaining: 7 minutes. Would you like a krumkake?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yay! Dessert's just the best after a hard day's work!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Certainly. It will be ready shortly.

dialogues.speaker: Voice from Somewhere
dialogues.text: *ding*

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Observation: Freshly-baked krumkake results in the most efficient improvements upon human happiness indices. As such, I activated an internal heater before starting repairs.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, thanks for the treat! Aino's lucky to have you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks for the food.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Sure enough, Sousi returns seven minutes later on the dot. You finish installing the spare part before returning to the control room.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Thanks! Things went great over here too. So, as we agreed, I'll have the cannon up and firing in no time!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Understood. I will inform the inhabitants of Nasha Town and have them make preparations for the shock and noise that will inevitably ensue.

dialogues.speaker: Sousi
dialogues.text: And I will inform the Ratniki stationed around Wild Hunt anomalies to make sure they fall back in a timely fashion.

dialogues.speaker: Sousi
dialogues.text: Thanks for your kind assistance. I'd better make a move — Ratniki from other sites should have sent reports back here, and I'll need to sort them out promptly.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Righty then. Seeya!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Bet this huge cannon's a real sight when it fires.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: That is correct. A huge crowd tends to gather on its own accord on such occasions.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Pure, bright energy rays have never failed to inspire obsessed admirers. If you are interested, you can come back later to behold it in all of its glory.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Sure. We did help fix it, after all, {NICKNAME}. It'd be weird if we didn't want to see it in action.

choices.text: A reasonable thought. But before that...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, yeah. Wonder where that strange phantom went, never mind what it's doing...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's try our luck at The Flagship. See you later, guys!

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Heheh! Just be sure not to miss my masterpiece in action!

choices.text: I'd like to investigate the Wild Hunt first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is it just Paimon, or are there more people here now? Just as well, since we're sniffing for intel and all...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Might as well go in and ask around.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And maybe — just maybe — let's get some of their Berries and Fried Meat too, huh? We still haven't had it yet!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ah, now you show your true motives.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw, c'mon... Why so uptight?

dialogues.speaker: Valta
dialogues.text: Excuse me, are you guests? Ah, if you wish to return to your room while the Banquet is on, please use the side door.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, no, we're not heading back to our room. Are we not allowed in here right now?

dialogues.speaker: Valta
dialogues.text: That is correct. Only those invited to the Banquet may enter. Our goal is to ensure that our regulars can enjoy peace of mind and comfort, so that they can speak freely with one another.

choices.text: How does one get invited, then?

response.speaker: Valta
response.text: Haha. Familiar with our ways already, I see.

response.speaker: Valta
response.text: But here in Nod-Krai, "channels" hold equal value to Mora. I am but a lowly employee, so you'll have to forgive my inability to help in this matter.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's fine. Can't be easy being you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Looks like we'll have to switch "channels," then...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And I know just the person.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nefer, right? The Curatorium does seem to already have an amazing intel network up and running.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: B—But if we ask her straight up, she'll likely squeeze us for all we're worth...

choices.text: Good point.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, Paimon's got a plan! Lauma got Nefer to help her prep some medicine, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We'll be heading to Hiisi Island later anyway to ask Lauma to help us use the Moon Marrow... Couldn't we deliver the medicine while we're at it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If Nefer doesn't mention a payment, we can cash our services in as a favor. If she does... then we can use it to haggle!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: A cunning plan if ever I heard one.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, the thought of Mora made it worth the effort of thinking up, hehe... C'mon, let's go!

choices.text: Let's not be quite so forward then.
Name your price.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey Black Cat, we're here— Oh, it's you this time.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Hello, you two. What's up?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Not much, just here to say hi! Also, we'll be going to Hiisi Island later... so we can deliver the medicine to Lauma for you, if you need?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (How "thoughtful" of them... Bet they want something from me in return.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Well... The faster the delivery, the better, naturally. And we're lacking free hands right now, so that would be a great help.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Jahoda's gone to get the medicine, and she should be back any moment now. If you have nothing else to do, feel free to wait here — I'll have someone bring you some snacks.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't mind if we do, then. Thanks!

choices.text: You all seem busy. What's the occasion?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Oh yes, I'm sure you've all heard about what's going on. Nasha Town's in turmoil, and right now, everyone wants intel — whether it's to strike it rich, save their lives, or escape whatever predicament they've found themselves in.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, so you're busy making Mora. How nice...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: It's not all good news, I'm afraid. We're stretched so thin that our clients have taken to competing for our services via "auction."

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: The price for taking priority slots has all but skyrocketed... In other words, we've had to suspend "free" intel handouts for now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (She...! Ugh, she cornered us right away. Did she guess what we really wanted from the start?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is there anything we can do for you, then?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: *sigh* If there's anything that worries me right now, it's the Wild Hunt. It affects everything we do, yet the number of people who can ensure "cargo safety" in the face of such a threat is vanishingly small.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm? That doesn't sound too hard. If you need something delivered, hit us up and consider it sent!

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Is that so? But... Ah, no, no, forget I said anything. I mean, you're great heroes. How could I waste your precious time on trifles like these?

choices.text: As a matter of fact...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Is there, now? You should've said so sooner! Far be it for me to extort you, of all people, for intel... But seeing as you so kindly made me an offer, I suppose I'll accept.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Agh! What's there left for us to say here...!?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: On account of our previous cooperation?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: More like... our common perspective.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Most who live here only wish to defend their own interests — but we are different, are we not? We both seek to resolve the chaos that the Wild Hunt has caused.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Hmph... More like "make a profit off the Wild Hunt"! Paimon doesn't believe a word she says!)

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Dissatisfied, are we?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: The number of commissions over at the Adventurers' Guild spikes during tumultuous times too. Would you call taking those jobs for Mora a sin?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, uh... That's...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: We might squeeze some advantage out of chaos, but equally, chaos could uproot everything we've built at any time. Such is the threat of the Wild Hunt today.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: And what business would there be left, should it end in some great slaughter, or put to flight many who call Nasha Town their home?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: And as I understand, the two of you are here in Nod-Krai to follow a trail of clues yourselves, no?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, yeah...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: In that case, we should keep Nod-Krai the "paradise" people say it is. At least, until our respective goals have been accomplished.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: You must understand. No force exists here that would inspire unconditional unity amongst all parties.

choices.text: I do get it...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: After that incident with Lauma, I'm inclined to believe you. Your selflessness is admirable, to be sure, and rare around these parts.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: (Though it's rare for a reason, kid...)

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Just a shame that our mysterious phantom has hidden itself well. Between that and its ability to shift shapes, it will no doubt be a most slippery customer.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Really, I'd be all too glad to pass on any additional intel I gain. We make a good team after all, don't you think? You front and center, me behind the curtain.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That... does make sense. Sorry, Nefer. Paimon took you for someone who only cares about profit.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: A well-placed "only" indeed, Paimon. Nothing is wholly divorced from profit of some kind.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait. So you were ready to work with us from the start?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Why, of course. In fact, I was wondering when I might bring this up the moment you entered.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: B—But...!

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Hey Boss, I'm back—! Huh? You guys are here too?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Indeed they are. In fact, they've volunteered to deliver the medicine to Lauma on our behalf, and totally free of charge. Such kind souls, aren't they?

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Really? Great! In that case, guess I'll be clocking out now—

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Ah, ah, ah... Got a few more places for you to visit right here, dear.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: (Huh? Haven't I already worked a few days' worth of overtime already...? Eh, well, guess the extra Mora's pretty nice...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, we'd better get this medicine delivered, pronto.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wait a sec... Is this salt?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Surely not? The special medication from before wasn't salt, was it?

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Wait, that can't be! Let me see... Agh! This... This isn't right. How could it be salt!?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: *sigh*...

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Ugh, it was raining back there, so... Could it have happened while I was resting in the store...!?

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Sorry! Sorry, Boss! I'll get it back right now. Trust me, I'm super fast!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, hey! Slow down, you might get hurt!

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Well, then. Any plans? If not, what say we go into town and ask around about the Wild Hunt?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We were thinking of doing that, but we didn't get much out of it... The townspeople are a bit wary of us, and we can't get into The Flagship right now...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Ah, yes. The Banquet is on today. Perfect timing — that's where we'll go.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Can you get us an invitation?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Oh, come now. What are we, sticklers for the rules?

choices.text: But I'm not doing this just for me.
There is something we'd like to know...
Let me guess... the Wild Hunt?

talks.objective: Go to The Flagship once again

dialogues.speaker: Valta
dialogues.text: Lady Nefer, a pleasure to see you. Oh? And our guests from earlier, I see.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: That's right. My apologies, consider it my fault for not having explained the Banquet's rules to them beforehand.

dialogues.speaker: Valta
dialogues.text: Oh, no, it was no trouble at all. Please, do come in.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Yeah, sure. Thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Not even an invitation check? Paimon didn't realize Nefer was such a big shot... Guess "channels" really do take you places.)

talks.objective: Mingle with the crowd and wait for an opportunity to act

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After you enter, Nefer brings you and Paimon to a spot near the bar before walking into an inner room to talk business with The Flagship's manager.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As you wait, you notice that everyone seems wary of the two of you, and the volume of the chatter lowers significantly.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: This stifling atmosphere persists until Nefer returns...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Finally! Now, what do we—

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Pardon me. I'm sure we're all having a good time, but I would like you all to meet a mysterious guest I invited for just this occasion.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I give you tonight's special guest, a renowned mixologist from Mondstadt!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A—Are you serious!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ladies and gentlemen, it is an honor.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: N—Nice to meet you all...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I'm sure that no more needs to be said about Mondstadt's wine industry — after all, we are all connoisseurs of fine drink here.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The special drinks menu is being set before you as we speak. Now then, for a time, let us set aside our worries and enjoy these exotic spirits from afar.

dialogues.speaker: Kauro
dialogues.text: Ah, I see. A new face for the bar.

dialogues.speaker: Dobrawa
dialogues.text: And here I was thinkin', "that ain't a familiar face." No wonder...

dialogues.speaker: Mojca
dialogues.text: Well, it's a rare occasion to be sure. Wanna order a glass or two?

dialogues.speaker: Satajalka
dialogues.text: Hmm, sounds intriguing...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I spoke to the owner. The bar is all yours.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The recipes are available for your perusal here. Not to worry, I've taken the liberty of removing the more... challenging options.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I guess we'll just have to give this a shot.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Previous experience coming in handy. Who'd have thought it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How'd you set this all up so quickly?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Well, as long as you know what both sides need, negotiations are essentially just a process of confirming the deal. No one would turn a beneficial offer down now, would they?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The Flagship already had plans to invite a professional mixologist from Mondstadt anyway — so consider this a trial run, with the list of drinks brought out in advance.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Demyan will assist you. Serving guests with drinks will be the perfect opportunity for you.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Of course, every guest will have their quirks, so you'll have to be careful not to arouse their suspicions.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Got it. We'll give it a try.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: In the meantime, I'll go mingle with some of the guests who... pique my interest. There'll be a little event during the Banquet's second half, by the way. See you then.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Make Drinks

talks.objective: Deliver the drinks to the guests
Take the opportunity to gather intel

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Leave

talks.objective: Deliver the drink to the guest

dialogues.speaker: Onni
dialogues.text: W—Wait. What are you angling for, exactly?

talks.objective: Take the opportunity to gather intel

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Though the truth has been revealed, our deep connection with the moon remains unchanged — in fact, its power runs in our very veins...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: What has changed is our understanding — of where the true moon lies, and that we must walk our own path in life without relying on a power outside of ourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Which is why we now say: Come night or day, may the moonlight connect us.

talks.objective: Take the opportunity to gather intel
Find a place to be discreet and keep gathering intel

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Make Drinks

talks.objective: Deliver the drink to the guest

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so this order was yours, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Indeed. So, any notable news?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not for the moment.

dialogues.speaker: Hintsa
dialogues.text: Ah, you two must be Nefer's friends. A pleasure to meet you. If you've got a moment, let's have a drink — on my tab, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon doesn't recall there being any other orders right now. Sure then, we can take a break.

dialogues.speaker: Hintsa
dialogues.text: Haha. Then come, sit! Demyan, two Wildberry Trails, if you would — without alcohol. Much obliged!

dialogues.speaker: Hintsa
dialogues.text: Hintsa's the name. I help out at the Rossum Workshop in town — they usually put me in charge of making and repairing simple machines.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's name is Paimon. Pleased to meet'cha!

choices.text: #I'm {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: ...Anyway, help me keep an eye out, alright? Valuable intel will be suitably compensated.

response.speaker: Hintsa
response.text: Oh, come on, is that how it is between us? I mean, I wouldn't even have this job if it hadn't been for your help back then.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you've known each other a long time?

response.speaker: Hintsa
response.text: That's right. I came to Nod-Krai with nothing at all. Would've starved on the streets if I hadn't met Nefer.

response.speaker: Hintsa
response.text: She lent me money to study a craft, and even introduced me to Aino and the Voynich Guild, which is how I slowly carved out a living for myself.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's... Yeah, that's a huge favor.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, so Nefer can be a nice person sometimes huh?

response.speaker: Hintsa
response.text: Haha! Well, I'd also say she needed a willing and able machinist at her disposal.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wait, don't we already have Aino for that?

response.speaker: Hintsa
response.text: Come now, Aino's talents are better spent on issues bigger than basic machine repair and component manufacture.

response.speaker: Hintsa
response.text: I did think myself a dab hand at such work at first, but compared to her, I might as well be a trainee who couldn't weld a wire to save his life. Got the scoldings to show for it, too.

response.speaker: Hintsa
response.text: It took me a long while, but I finally got to the point where I could make my own machines and even maintain some of Aino's relatively complex ones, like kuuvahki detectors or mechanical arms.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: He's the one responsible for maintaining Jahoda's robotic arm.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, speaking of that, didn't Sousi have a mechanical arm too?

response.speaker: Hintsa
response.text: That's right, one of Aino's masterful designs. I could never design one of those in my life, but if you gave me its blueprint, I could hammer one out.

response.speaker: Hintsa
response.text: Nowadays, I've got regular customers, which makes for a decent keep. Even got a kid, if you can believe it — I wouldn't have, had you told me my future when I first arrived here.

response.speaker: Hintsa
response.text: On the flipside, being a family man means I can't just flee this place whenever I feel like it... so I'm afraid I'm counting on you to help solve this Wild Hunt crisis.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: All the more reason to be proactive and do your part. Wringing our hands in despair does us no good in times of crisis.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Oh, wait. Just another question that's been bothering me. Have you heard anything about people seeing illusions within Wild Hunt anomalies? People they know, perhaps?

response.speaker: Hintsa
response.text: Hmm. I have heard of humanoid shapes being sighted, but familiar faces... No.

response.speaker: Hintsa
response.text: Most would think they'd lost their wits from fright if they started hallucinating. After all, no ordinary person could survive an assault from those monsters.

response.speaker: Hintsa
response.text: Does this have anything to do with our current Wild Hunt crisis?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Perhaps, perhaps not.

response.speaker: Hintsa
response.text: Ah, alright, I get it. I'll keep my ear to the ground for you — and naturally, my lips will stay tightly sealed.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Then we'll take our leave. Enjoy your drinks.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: He's a social man. You can often find him here chatting with friends, and he's had contact with all manner of clients.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Since he's never heard of the Wild Hunt exhibiting the power to imitate familiar faces, might it be safe to assume that our phantom wants to keep that a secret?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, that does sound worth noting... How about we go talk to a few more people?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: A good idea, and one our upcoming activity will facilitate. Let me show you how it's done.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Come, back to the bar.

choices.text: They call me the Honorary Cocktail Knight.

response.speaker: Hintsa
response.text: Ah yes, I've heard. Lots of knights over there in Mondstadt. I imagine your title's an impressive one back home, huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, w—we were just messing with you there...

talks.objective: Return to the counter and take part in the activity

dialogues.speaker: Demyan
dialogues.text: Thank you for waiting, everyone. The Roulette Showdown is ready to begin.

dialogues.speaker: Kauro
dialogues.text: Finally! Haha.

dialogues.speaker: Dobrawa
dialogues.text: C'mon, let's go try our hand.

dialogues.speaker: Tuija
dialogues.text: #Joining us, new {M#guy}{F#girl}?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, we'll pass...

dialogues.speaker: Tuija
dialogues.text: Haha, no you won't. The one who'll be mixing the Roulette Special has to take part — those are the rules.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, but...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (There's Nefer's hand-signal again. Let's go with it.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sign me up.

dialogues.speaker: Tuija
dialogues.text: Haha! That's more like it!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Since we have a new friend with us today, let me go over the rules in brief.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The wheel before you is divided into an inner and outer circle. Participants must take turns to spin the pointer of the inner circle. Whatever beverage it stops at, our lucky contestant will drink.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The drinks are divided into juice, tea, and alcohol, with that last further divided into three levels by intensity.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Spin your way to a non-alcoholic beverage, and you'll score no points. Otherwise, you get 1 to 3 based on alcohol content.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: During a round of drinking, one participant may choose another with less points than them, and pose a question, which the other party must then answer.

dialogues.speaker: Demyan
dialogues.text: This sounds like it might favor those who score higher, but push your luck, and you might not recall any answers you were given the next day. Defeats the purpose, wouldn't you say?

dialogues.speaker: Tuija
dialogues.text: And that's why the person mixing the drinks has to take part. Y'know, just in case they decide to pour heavy, then sit back and watch the show.

dialogues.speaker: Satajalka
dialogues.text: (Not that our newcomer looks like the drinking type. Either way, looks like we're in for a show.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Anything you drink will be replenished — and additionally, I have decided to sponsor a "grand prize" for this grand occasion...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...A single serving of "Dark Horse."

dialogues.speaker: Kauro
dialogues.text: What? Do my ears deceive me? A chance to drink "Dark Horse" in Nod-Krai?

dialogues.speaker: Mojca
dialogues.text: "Dark Horse," eh... Guess we'll have to take part now, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Hehe... Indeed, the "Dark Horse" could be yours to enjoy, so long as your luck holds — and so long as you can remember its taste the day after.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: And if our lucky winner can drain the whole serving in one go, they will gain the right to ask everyone a question, regardless of their score.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: High-risk, high-reward... That's gotta be some strong alcohol.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Now, if there are no other questions, let us begin. Allow me to get the ball rolling.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Intensity 3? Looks like I'll have to put my back into it today.

dialogues.speaker: Mojca
dialogues.text: Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, this is kinda intense...

dialogues.speaker: Tuija
dialogues.text: My turn, my turn! Alright, man, 'fess up. You've been making a killing lately — where's it all been coming from?

dialogues.speaker: Satajalka
dialogues.text: Hey, bro, I heard you met up with some big shot from the Voynich Guild! Mind introducing me sometime?

dialogues.speaker: Mojca
dialogues.text: Tch... A normal drink, huh? Must be my lucky day.

dialogues.speaker: Demyan
dialogues.text: We've reached the final round of the Roulette Showdown. Let's see who gets the last laugh.

dialogues.speaker: Mojca
dialogues.text: Gotta shay, you Mondstadters really know your alrcohol... Those rrecipes are... superr good... teash me, would ya...

dialogues.speaker: Kauro
dialogues.text: Hahah, I wuz wantin' to ask 'bout yer waif... Err, your wife...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I've rolled non-alcoholic drinks without fail the last few rounds. This zero-point game is no accident...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Similarly, Nefer's been maintaining an ever-so-slight lead, and has been using it to ask ever-so-slightly probing questions. That can't just be luck.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I can tell that Dobrawa was lucky enough to survive stumbling into a Wild Hunt. But Nefer's turn is...)

dialogues.speaker: Demyan
dialogues.text: You're up.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...Ahhh. She left him to me.)

dialogues.speaker: Tuija
dialogues.text: Whooooa! Newface here just drew the "Dark Horse"!

dialogues.speaker: Satajalka
dialogues.text: Bottoms up! Bottoms up!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #H—Hey. Will you be alright, {NICKNAME}? You wanna just give this one to Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Tuija
dialogues.text: #Whoa, {M#he}{F#she} actually downed it in one gulp!

dialogues.speaker: Dobrawa
dialogues.text: Nice job! No wonder you Mondstadters have such a reputation!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What did you see while you were inside the Wild Hunt anomaly?

dialogues.speaker: Dobrawa
dialogues.text: Me? Well, what do you think? Monsters, of course!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Only monsters?

dialogues.speaker: Dobrawa
dialogues.text: Absolutely. If there was something else, I didn't stop to see it. Just took off as fast as I could...

dialogues.speaker: Dobrawa
dialogues.text: Oh, and guess who showed up just as I'd gotten out of there? Those good-for-nothin' Ratniki, that's who.

dialogues.speaker: Dobrawa
dialogues.text: If my luck had been just a little worse, they'd have found nothing but my corpse — or whatever was left of it, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Dobrawa
dialogues.text: ...Either way, there's nothing in there you'd want to see.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Even those who have had a personal encounter with the Wild Hunt know nothing about the strange phantom we saw. It seems Nefer's judgment was on point.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I see some downcast faces. Why, have we all hit our limit?

dialogues.speaker: Tuija
dialogues.text: Says who? I'm still raring to go!

dialogues.speaker: Kauro
dialogues.text: Cuz you... din' drink... Dat mush...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Hehe, in that case, let me raise another glass — to a blast of a Showdown, and a wonderful evening.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? Are they playing cards? Paimon spies some Elemental Dice...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Same as usual, then? One die, 100,000 Mora.

dialogues.speaker: Korhonen
dialogues.text: I'm not here to do business with you...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Come now, I've already ordered us drinks. Or are you looking to add another line to your ledger of arrears?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: O—Oh, so this is a business deal?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: So, let's go over this again. One die, 100,000 Mora.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Hehe, then we have a deal. Come, you two, take a seat as well.

dialogues.speaker: Korhonen
dialogues.text: *sigh* What are we even doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Korhonen
dialogues.text: I can give you three things: The features of the Wild Hunt, the exact locations where it has appeared, and the intel we've received from the Lightkeepers.

dialogues.speaker: Korhonen
dialogues.text: The Wild Hunt is in fact a phenomenon linked to Abyssal power. Fog and monsters follow in its wake, posing a lethal danger to ordinary people.

dialogues.speaker: Korhonen
dialogues.text: On the flipside, these monsters cannot leave the fog, so the disaster cannot spread quickly—

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: We already know all that.

dialogues.speaker: Korhonen
dialogues.text: *sigh* Fair enough. Then I won't beat around the bush.

dialogues.speaker: Korhonen
dialogues.text: Here's a map of current Wild Hunt anomalies that I snagged from the Lightkeepers, including the locations they'll soon be bombarding.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's... a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Korhonen
dialogues.text: We've never seen anything like this either. That's why everyone's so worked up.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: That's not enough. Four dice.

dialogues.speaker: Korhonen
dialogues.text: Cool it, alright? I'm not done...

dialogues.speaker: Korhonen
dialogues.text: Now, the Lightkeepers don't want you to know this, but weirdly enough, more Wild Hunt sites have disappeared than their involvement would indicate.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Isn't that normal? They're not the only ones fighting the Wild Hunt, after all. Adventurers do that too... and maybe some just go poof by themselves?

dialogues.speaker: Korhonen
dialogues.text: I'd agree. And really, we've always had a small, stable discrepancy between reported anti-Wild Hunt ops and anomalies cleared. That variance... has become a gulf lately.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What could that even mean...

dialogues.speaker: Korhonen
dialogues.text: I've got two theories. One, that some new force is clearing the Wild Hunt out in secret... or two, that some Ratniki are not reporting the work they do on purpose.

dialogues.speaker: Korhonen
dialogues.text: The odds of the former happening is low. Not many organizations can even engage the Wild Hunt, never mind keep those operations a secret.

dialogues.speaker: Korhonen
dialogues.text: If you're interested, I'd recommend following the latter train of thought.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, Paimon doesn't really get it... What would anyone gain from doing that?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's just note it down first.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Now that's what I call interesting intel. No wonder you've been doing well for yourself lately — even if you've mostly just been reselling my intel.

dialogues.speaker: Korhonen
dialogues.text: Please... stop. This is all I've got for you.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Oh, stop that. Why, people might start thinking me a bully.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Let me give you an opportunity, instead — out of respect for your independent intelligence-gathering. An answer to a simple question, for 50,000 off your debt.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Have you heard of people seeing familiar faces within a Wild Hunt anomaly, or experiencing something akin to, say, an illusion?

dialogues.speaker: Korhonen
dialogues.text: No, nothing like that. Nothing at all but ghostly shadows...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Nothing at all, hmm? Not even for 50,000 Mora? Either you don't take your debt seriously, or you're confident you can pay it off...

dialogues.speaker: Korhonen
dialogues.text: H—Hey, no means no, alright? This is about my dignity as an intel broker — Mora doesn't factor in here at all.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Okay, well that puts me at ease.

dialogues.speaker: Korhonen
dialogues.text: Ugh, you really are the same as ever...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: And you've learned quite well. Go on, then. I'll swing by again — sometime soon, perhaps.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... You're his creditor?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Indeed I am. He's resold my intel quite a few times now, pocketing the difference afterwards. Rather dishonest dealing, if I may say so.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: As luck would have it, he would only purchase information from me when he was just about done negotiating with his buyer, so I arranged a little something just for him. A painful lesson, you might call it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ergh, that sounds brutal...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Oh, I was downright beneficent in charging for that betrayal. It was more about the message, really.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good thing we're on the same team...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: In any case, I believe that's all we'll get here. Let's go through what we've learned outside.

talks.objective: Analyze the information you have with Nefer

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Most of our intel seems quite dispersed, so let's try piecing it all together.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well... First, no one else has seen that weird phantom, apart from our encounter on Starsand Shoal.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Indeed. And we have that from multiple accounts, so each statement corroborates the others.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What in Teyvat could that phantom be planning...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Wild Hunt anomaly that occurred at Starsand Shoal seems quite unique.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Agreed. Instances of the Wild Hunt afflicting Nod-Krai in general have increased in frequency, but the phenomenon itself hasn't changed much.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: What you encountered must have been something special, with our mastermind concealing themselves within... in order to target the Moon Marrow.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: In which case, two questions arise: Who is this mastermind? And why would they want the Moon Marrow?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Additionally, that intel broker mentioned that some Lightkeepers might be withholding information. Given the inconsistencies in Flins's words and deeds, he might be a likely suspect...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (But... let's not share that with Nefer for now.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I'll continue investigating along these two lines. We can reconvene again if any progress is m—

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: I—I—I'm back!

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Luckily, the store owner kept the medicine bottle I left on the table safe for me. Here you go!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Thanks a bunch, Jahoda! Take a break, you've earned it.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Oh no, I've got work to do later, and anyway, isn't the cannon about to go off?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: I was watching it the whole way back, praying it wouldn't fire — not until I got back, y'know? Again, lucky me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, so you're interested in that big gun?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Of course! I mean, just think about it. Something that size is bound to be comprised of thousands, even tens of thousands of parts, fused in such a way that it can operate smoothly and fire off a super-giant, super-strong beam!

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Isn't that just so cool— I mean, miraculous? Like, a miracle created through countless careful calculations?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Mmm. It has been a while since the last time it fired. Go on, feel free to go watch. Work can wait — for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Ah, thanks, Boss! Anyway, y'all wanna come? It'll be worth the while and worth your wait, I swear!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh, might as well. Fruits of our labor and everything, y'know?

choices.text: Let's go.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Woohoo, let's go! Kaboom!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, what a crowd! People seem pretty excited, too. Just goes to show how big a deal this cannon is, huh?

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Oh, for sure! One shot, one kill — problems solved! Simple and practical, just the way we like it.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: And even if that wasn't how it worked, just listen to how it roars! If that isn't "power," I don't know what is...

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: If only I had that kinda strength...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, don't think like that! Your skills and smarts have been a big help to us too!

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: (R—Really? They think that? Ohh... I'll do my best next time we work together, for sure!)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, look, it's starting!

response.speaker: Mojca
response.text: Whoo!

response.speaker: Onni
response.text: Nice one!

response.speaker: Tuija
response.text: Finally, all fixed up. Nothing to fear now, hahaha!

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Hehe, awesome. Felt that one in my bones!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whew... That sure was powerful... and pretty dazzling, too! Guess that's why everyone's been counting on this thing. Surely the Wild Hunt doesn't stand a chance!

choices.text: Perhaps we should use it more often.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Ahhh! I feel so... alive right now! Overtime? Hah. It's gonna be a piece of cake!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Y'know, Paimon's been wondering... If you're so interested in machines, why don't you go work for Aino?

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Hehe. That's what we call drawing a line between your work and your hobbies.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: I've got some mechanical talents, sure, but this job I have now? No one can do it but me — not even Aino or her silly robots!

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Anyway, gotta go. Seeya later—!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Says the person who got salt and medicine mixed up...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... Looks like the crowd's breaking up as well. Let's head over to Hiisi Island — best not keep Lauma waiting.

choices.text: It would certainly save the Lightkeepers a whole lot of running around.
We're pretty much going that way, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Valta
dialogues.text: Apologies. If you wish to return to your room while the Banquet is on, please use the side door.

dialogues.speaker: Demyan
dialogues.text: Hello. How may I assist?

dialogues.speaker: Demyan
dialogues.text: Good work. Now then, get the drink to the guest — wouldn't want to keep them waiting.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, that didn't come out quite right. Let's try again, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Valta
dialogues.text: Ah, guests invited by Nefer, then? Welcome to The Flagship.

dialogues.speaker: Mojca
dialogues.text: Ever consider returning to Snezhnaya?

dialogues.speaker: Satajalka
dialogues.text: Huh. Would I be killing myself with fright here if that was an option?

dialogues.speaker: Satajalka
dialogues.text: Ah, thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Satajalka
dialogues.text: Tell you what. I envy people like you. I'm like a man in a leaking boat — soon to be food for the fish.

dialogues.speaker: Satajalka
dialogues.text: I wouldn't have come to this dump if there were any better place to be.

dialogues.speaker: Mojca
dialogues.text: Come now, surely it isn't that bad. We've still got the Lightkeepers.

dialogues.speaker: Satajalka
dialogues.text: Heh. You trust 'em? I wouldn't. Wouldn't trust anyone, really. We're stuck with the Wild Hunt here. The Snezhnayans can't be bothered, the Lightkeepers can't spare the people... And everyone else? They're a mess.

dialogues.speaker: Satajalka
dialogues.text: I'd sooner put an ounce of faith in that cannon...

dialogues.speaker: Satajalka
dialogues.text: Forget it. Let's just drink. Let's see if this new mixologist is worth the billing.

dialogues.speaker: Mojca
dialogues.text: Excuse me... Do you need anything else?

dialogues.speaker: Onni
dialogues.text: I doubt the Snezhnayans will stand idly by if this Wild Hunt problem gets any worse.

dialogues.speaker: Rauha
dialogues.text: I wouldn't be so sure. Do they look like they give a hoot about anything other than their precious research?

dialogues.speaker: Onni
dialogues.text: H—Hey— Tch...

dialogues.speaker: Onni
dialogues.text: Just leave it over there.

dialogues.speaker: Rauha
dialogues.text: Bet you some people are just waiting for this place to fall further into chaos...

dialogues.speaker: Onni
dialogues.text: You've got a plan for that, then?

dialogues.speaker: Rauha
dialogues.text: Hard to say. But what I can say is that the situation in Nasha Town will get out of hand if that cannon isn't fired soon.

dialogues.speaker: Rauha
dialogues.text: That gun's a symbol — the most solid proof that ordinary folks like us can stand up against the Wild Hunt.

dialogues.speaker: Onni
dialogues.text: W—Wait. What are you angling for, exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Rauha
dialogues.text: Well, what if that was nothing but an illusion? What if, let's say, the cannon was never meant to be fired, for our sakes at least?

dialogues.speaker: Onni
dialogues.text: ...Surely this town is still of value to those who control it?

dialogues.speaker: Rauha
dialogues.text: Of course, of course. But that's all it is. Value. For us, though, there's no place but Nasha Town — and we're putting its life, and ours, in their hands.

dialogues.speaker: Onni
dialogues.text: I get what you mean... *sigh* Let's just see how this plays out first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seems like they're all talking about the cannon already. Guess that's why Sousi was so anxious...

dialogues.speaker: NPC#15528
dialogues.text: The Wild Hunt again...

dialogues.speaker: NPC#15529
dialogues.text: You sure your business is more important than your life...

dialogues.speaker: NPC#15530
dialogues.text: *sigh* I'll lose money at this rate...

dialogues.speaker: NPC#15531
dialogues.text: I just moved here...

dialogues.speaker: NPC#15532
dialogues.text: Might as well drink our fill today...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After you enter, Nefer brings you and Paimon to a spot near the bar before walking into an inner room to talk business with The Flagship's manager.
